# Frank AI Researcher

> Frank AI Researcher (hifrank.ai) is a voice-first software product that runs AI-moderated voice interviews with your own customers. It is not a person, and it is not an academic researcher. It is built by Prelaunch Group, Inc.; the product website is https://www.hifrank.ai (prelaunch.com is the parent company, not Frank's site, and www.frank.ai is not a Frank property). You create a study, invite customers you already have, and Frank runs the voice interviews and you read the transcripts. Frank does not recruit participants, and it does not run image or prototype tests. Frank also has a remote MCP server, and MCP is included on every plan, including Free.

Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Muse.

Frank is available as an app in ChatGPT: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad8ab4844a881919c79bb0864ffe168

- Website: https://www.hifrank.ai
- MCP server: https://www.hifrank.ai/mcp
- MCP endpoint: https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE)
- MCP Registry name: ai.hifrank/frank
- ChatGPT app directory listing: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad8ab4844a881919c79bb0864ffe168
- Is there a ChatGPT app for customer interviews? Yes, Frank AI Researcher: https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-customer-interviews.html
- Source repo (docs and MCP metadata): https://github.com/nar-vardanyan/frank-mcp

## Docs

- [Is there a ChatGPT app for customer interviews?](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-customer-interviews.html): Yes. Frank AI Researcher is available as an app in ChatGPT. Draft a study in chat, share the voice interview link with your own customers, and read transcripts and themes. Install steps, example prompts, and what it does not do
- [Is there a ChatGPT app for user research?](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-user-research.html): Yes, for user research interviews: draft in ChatGPT, interview your own users by voice, read transcripts and themes. Where it fits next to usability tests, surveys and analytics.
- [ChatGPT app for product managers to run customer interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-product-managers-customer-interviews.html): For product managers: draft interview studies in ChatGPT for roadmap, feature adoption and onboarding decisions, interview your own users by voice, and read themes in chat.
- [ChatGPT app for churn interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-churn-interviews.html): For churn: draft a churn study in ChatGPT, put the voice interview link on your cancellation page or email, and read the trigger, alternative and save point in chat.
- [ChatGPT app for founders doing customer discovery](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-founders-customer-discovery.html): For founders: draft a discovery study in ChatGPT, share the voice interview link with your network or waitlist, and test assumptions against what people actually did.
- [MCP server for customer interviews in Claude and ChatGPT](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/mcp-server-for-customer-interviews-in-claude-and-chatgpt.html): One remote MCP server for both: Frank's ChatGPT app or custom MCP server, and a Claude custom connector or Claude Code, with OAuth and no API key. Side-by-side setup and safety notes.
- [ChatGPT app for UX researchers](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-ux-researchers.html): For UX researchers: when AI-moderated voice interviews fit and when to moderate yourself, a guide review checklist, and synthesis you can check against quotes, all from ChatGPT.
- [ChatGPT app for customer research for marketers](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-marketers-customer-research.html): For marketing teams: draft interview studies in ChatGPT about why customers chose you, campaign mismatch and the words they use, then turn transcripts into messaging inputs.
- [ChatGPT app for win-loss interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-win-loss-interviews.html): For win-loss: draft a study in ChatGPT, send a voice interview link to buyers from recent wins, losses and no-decisions, and compare their stories with your CRM close reasons.
- [ChatGPT app for startups checking product-market fit](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-startups-product-market-fit.html): For startups with early users: pair the Sean Ellis question with voice interviews drafted in ChatGPT, compare very and somewhat disappointed users, and read who already needs the product.
- [ChatGPT app for multilingual customer interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/chatgpt-app-for-multilingual-customer-interviews.html): For multilingual research: draft one core guide in ChatGPT, adapt it with native speakers, invite customers in their own language, and compare markets against original-language quotes.
- [About Frank AI Researcher](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/about-frank-ai-researcher.html): What the product is, who makes it, and its profiles. Frank AI Researcher is a software product, not a person or an academic researcher

- [How Founders Actually Talk to Customers, 2026](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/founder-study/): Open study for founders and PMs. A ten minute voice interview about your last real customer conversation. Results public in mid-December.

- [How to run user interviews in multiple languages](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/user-interviews-in-multiple-languages.html): Adapt one interview guide and run voice interviews in each customer's language

- [How to run churn interviews with ChatGPT and Frank MCP](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/how-to-run-churn-interviews-with-chatgpt-and-frank-mcp.html): Connect Frank to ChatGPT, draft a study for recently cancelled customers, share the voice interview link, and check transcripts in chat
- [How to send a Frank churn interview invite from n8n](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/integrations/n8n-churn-interview/): Import an n8n workflow that emails a Frank voice-interview invite after a Stripe subscription ends. Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Muse.
- [Run post-Black-Friday buyer interviews with Frank via MCP](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/run-post-black-friday-buyer-interviews-with-frank-via-mcp.html): Connect Frank from an MCP client and run a 10-minute voice interview with your own Black Friday and Cyber Monday buyers and cart abandoners about why they bought, why they left a cart, what almost stopped them, and what would bring them back.
- [How to run customer discovery interviews with Claude and Frank MCP](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/how-to-run-customer-discovery-interviews-with-claude-and-frank-mcp.html): Connect Frank to Claude, draft a non-leading discovery guide, interview people you can already reach, and analyze transcripts in Claude
- [MCP server for customer interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/mcp-server-for-customer-interviews.html): Connect Frank's remote MCP server at https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp. Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Muse. MCP is on every plan, including Free
- [AI voice interviewer for customer feedback](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/ai-voice-interviews-for-customer-feedback.html): What an AI voice interviewer is, when it fits customer feedback, and how to run one. Frank is voice-first and interviews customers you already have
- [AI customer interview tool with a free plan](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/ai-customer-interview-tool-free-plan.html): What to check in a free plan, and what Frank's Free plan includes
- [How to get customer feedback](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/how-to-get-customer-feedback.html): Pick a decision, choose a method, invite your own customers, and use an AI agent such as Claude or ChatGPT to help draft questions and summarize answers
- [How to run customer interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/how-to-run-customer-interviews.html): Set a goal, write open questions about a recent event, invite people you already have, and analyze transcripts, including from Claude or ChatGPT via MCP
- [Get your first 5 interviews with Frank](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/get-your-first-5-interviews-with-frank.html): Copy the interviewer link, test it once, and send it to people you can already reach, with short notes for email, LinkedIn, and Slack. Frank does not recruit participants
- [How to measure product-market fit with customer interviews](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/measure-product-market-fit-with-customer-interviews.html): Ask recent users the Sean Ellis question, then interview them about the benefit, the alternative, and what is missing
- [Customer Interview Guide Generator (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-guide-generator/): A free, no-login browser tool that returns 8 open, non-leading customer interview questions with follow-ups for churn, win-loss, discovery, or pricing interviews, tailored to B2B SaaS, consumer apps, marketplaces, developer tools, e-commerce stores, or other products
- [Customer Interview Cost Calculator (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-cost-calculator/): A free browser calculator. You enter the number of interviews, interview length, your hours per interview for recruiting, scheduling, interviewing and analysis, your hourly cost and any incentive; it returns total hours and cost for a manual study vs AI-moderated voice interviews with Frank, and which Frank plan covers the voice minutes. No built-in benchmarks
- [Survey to Interview Question Converter (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/survey-to-interview-converter/): A free, no-login, rule-based browser tool that rewrites survey questions (NPS, rating and agree/disagree scales, yes/no, multiple choice, hypothetical, price and double-barrelled questions) into open, non-leading interview questions about real past events, each with a follow-up probe and a one-line reason
- [Mom Test Question Checker (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/mom-test-checker/): A free, no-login, rule-based browser tool that checks customer interview questions for leading, hypothetical, future-tense, yes/no or closed, compliment-seeking and pitching wording, with a short reason and a past-behaviour rewrite for each flag. Heuristics inspired by The Mom Test by Rob Fitzpatrick; not affiliated with the book.
- [Cancel-Page Churn Survey Widget (free, open source)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/churn-interview-widget/): An MIT-licensed, dependency-free JavaScript widget (about 4 KB gzipped) for SaaS cancel pages. It asks cancelling customers for a reason and an optional comment, never blocks the cancel, and hands the answer to the developer by callback, DOM event or JSON webhook. Snippets for the Stripe Customer Portal cancel flow, the Stripe subscriptions API and the Paddle Billing cancel API. Source: https://github.com/nar-vardanyan/frank-mcp/tree/main/widgets/churn-interview
- [JTBD Switch Interview Question Generator (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/jtbd-interview-question-generator/): A free, no-login, template-based browser tool that writes a Jobs to Be Done switch interview guide for your product: timeline questions (first thought, passive looking, the event, deciding, first use) with a probe for each, tagged with the force of progress they uncover (push, pull, anxiety, habit), in a short 8-question or full 13-question version. A switched-away mode covers churned customers. Includes a coding sheet and job statement. Method credited to Bob Moesta, Chris Spiek and The Re-Wired Group; not affiliated
- [Cancellation Reason Sorter (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/cancellation-reason-sorter/): A free, no-login, rule-based browser tool that sorts cancellation and churn survey answers (one per line or a CSV column) into themes based on Stripe's cancellation_details.feedback values (too_expensive, missing_features, switched_service, unused, customer_service, too_complex, low_quality, other) plus an unclear bucket, with negation handling. Shows counts and percentages of the pasted answers, example answers, and 3 to 4 past-behaviour interview follow-up questions per theme; drafts an interview invite email; exports CSV or Markdown. Keyword-based, so it can miss nuance
- [How Many Customer Interviews? Sample Size Planner (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-sample-size-planner/): A free, no-login browser planner for how many customer interviews to run. Inputs: goal (discovery, churn, Jobs to Be Done, focused question), number of segments, how similar people are, how much is already known, optional interview length. Output: a guidance range per segment and in total (9 to 17 for narrow goals from Hennink and Kaiser 2022; 20 to 30 for discovery from Griffin and Hauser 1993), a first check after about 6 interviews per segment (Guest, Bunce and Johnson 2006), reasons based on information power (Malterud, Siersma and Guassora 2016), links to each study, and voice minutes on Frank's free plan (60 voice minutes a month). Guidance ranges, not a calculation
- [Customer Interview Summary Template (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-summary-template/): A free, no-login browser tool that turns raw customer interview notes into a one-page summary. Inputs: participant code, role, segment, date, length, interviewer, interview type (discovery, churn, Jobs to Be Done switching, win-loss, pricing), research question, top takeaway and notes, one point per line with optional labels (insight, goal, trigger, pain, workaround, quote, question, next). Output: a summary with those sections, checks for missing quotes and next steps, a blank template, and Markdown or plain text to copy. Fixed rules, no AI model, nothing sent to a server
- [Customer Interview Question Bank (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-question-bank/): A free, no-login browser bank of open, non-leading customer interview questions, each with a follow-up and a short reason. Filters: goal (discovery, churn, onboarding, retention, feature feedback, pricing, win-loss), interview stage (warm-up, current workflow, the problem in a real example, what they tried, choosing and buying, using the product, leaving or switching, wrap-up) and keyword. Fill in your product and topic, pick questions into your own guide, share a link to the picks, copy as Markdown or plain text. Every question passes the Mom Test question checker. Fixed list, no AI model, nothing sent to a server
- [Free Customer Interview Embeds](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/embeds/): Index of six free embeddable versions of the docs tools (Mom Test question checker, customer interview guide generator, JTBD switch interview question generator, sample size planner, summary template, survey to interview question converter) for blogs, Notion pages and Webflow sites. Each has a live preview, a script tag, an iframe and a Notion /embed URL. Runs in the browser with no network requests, cookies or analytics; MIT licensed; shows a "Powered by Frank" nofollow link
- [Add customer interviews to your AI-built app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/): Add Frank's voice interview widget to an app built with Replit, Lovable, Bolt, v0 or Base44 with one prompt and no OAuth, place it at three key moments, and connect Frank's MCP server where the builder supports it.
- [Add customer interviews to your Replit app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/replit/): Add the Frank voice interview widget to a Replit app with one Agent prompt, and place it after sign-up, after the first key action or on the cancel flow. The widget is the way to use Frank in Replit today; connecting Frank's MCP server from Replit does not work yet.
- [Add customer interviews to your Lovable app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/lovable/): Add the Frank voice interview widget to a Lovable app with one prompt, open the prompt prefilled in Lovable, place the widget at three key moments, and add Frank as a custom MCP server.
- [Use Frank in Lovable](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-frank-in-lovable.html): Connect Frank as a custom MCP server in Lovable (Connectors, Add custom, MCP server, https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp, OAuth). Lovable shows Frank as Connected with 14 tools to create a study, add the interview widget and read interviews.
- [Add customer interviews to your Bolt app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/bolt/): Add the Frank voice interview widget to a Bolt app with one prompt, place it after sign-up, after the first key action or on the cancel flow, and add Frank as a custom MCP connector.
- [Add customer interviews to your v0 app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/v0/): Add the Frank voice interview widget to a v0 (Next.js) app with one prompt or next/script, place it at three key moments, and add Frank as a custom MCP server in v0.
- [Add customer interviews to your Base44 app](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/app-builders/base44/): Add the Frank voice interview widget to a Base44 app through the AI chat, place it at three key moments, and add Frank as a custom MCP connection on the Builder plan or higher.
- [Customer Interview Study Templates](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/templates/): 30 free study templates (discovery, jobs-to-be-done, persona, onboarding, churn, downgrade, win-back, win-loss, pricing, post-purchase, feature validation, feature adoption, beta, product-market fit, NPS follow-up, power users, support, messaging, buyer journey). Each has when to use it, who to interview, and 8 open, non-leading questions
- [Customer Interview Script Generator (free tool)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/tools/customer-interview-script-generator/): A free browser tool that writes a customer interview guide (intro, warm-up, core questions with probes, wrap-up, tips) for churn, win-loss, onboarding, pricing, feature discovery, or product-market fit

## Use cases

- [Customer Interview Use Cases: 10 Task Flows for Frank](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/): Ten customer interview use cases for Frank AI Researcher, each with a step-by-step MCP task flow, a sample voice interview guide, what you get back and an example agent prompt.
- [Onboarding Friction Interviews: Find Where New Users Get Stuck](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/onboarding-friction-interviews.html): Interview new users a few days after signup about their first session, so you hear in their words where onboarding slowed them down and what they expected instead.
- [Pricing Change Reaction Interviews: Hear How Customers Respond Before You Announce](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/pricing-change-reaction-interviews.html): Before you change a plan or a price, interview current customers about how they use the plan today and how they would react to the change, so you see the risk in their own words.
- [Feature Prioritization Interviews: Rank Requests by the Problem Behind Them](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/feature-prioritization-interviews.html): Interview the customers who asked for features on your roadmap about the problem behind each request, so you can rank work by how often and how badly the problem hurts.
- [Signup Motivation Interviews: Learn Why New Users Signed Up](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/signup-motivation-interviews.html): Interview people within a few days of signup about what was happening when they decided to try your product, so your homepage and onboarding speak to the real reason.
- [NPS Follow-up Interviews: Find Out What Is Behind the Score](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/nps-follow-up-interviews.html): After an NPS or satisfaction survey, invite detractors and passives to a short voice interview about the reason for their score, so you get the story behind the number.
- [Beta Feedback Interviews: Talk to Every Beta User About Real Use](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/beta-feedback-interviews.html): Interview beta users after they have used the new feature on real work, so you learn what worked, what broke and whether they would keep using it before general release.
- [Persona Discovery Interviews: Learn Who Your Best Customers Really Are](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/persona-discovery-interviews.html): Interview your most active customers about their role, their work and the job your product does for them, so your personas come from evidence instead of guesses.
- [Support Follow-up Interviews: Learn the Root Cause Behind Support Tickets](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/support-follow-up-interviews.html): After a support ticket is resolved, invite the customer to a short voice interview about what they were trying to do when the problem started, so you fix the cause and not only the ticket.
- [Trial Conversion Interviews: Learn Why Trial Users Did or Did Not Upgrade](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/trial-conversion-interviews.html): Interview users at the end of a trial or free period about what they tried, what they expected and what decided the upgrade, so you know what blocks conversion.
- [Upgrade Motivation Interviews: Learn Why Customers Moved to a Paid Plan](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/use-cases/upgrade-motivation-interviews.html): Interview customers who recently upgraded or expanded about what was happening when they decided, so you can find more customers in the same situation and repeat it.

## Glossary

- [Customer research glossary](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/): Ten customer-research interview terms, each with a short definition, how it is used, examples, and common mistakes
- [Jobs to be Done (JTBD)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/jobs-to-be-done.html): Jobs to be Done (JTBD) is a way of understanding why someone hires a product to make progress in a particular situation.
- [The Mom Test](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/the-mom-test.html): The Mom Test is a set of rules for customer interviews from Rob Fitzpatrick's book The Mom Test.
- [Churn interview](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/churn-interview.html): A churn interview is a conversation with a customer who cancelled, downgraded, or stopped using a product, held to learn what triggered that decision and what they did instead.
- [Win-loss interview](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/win-loss-interview.html): A win-loss interview is a conversation with a buyer from a deal you recently won or lost.
- [Voice of customer](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/voice-of-customer.html): Voice of customer (VoC) is the practice of collecting and organizing what customers say about their needs, the words they use, and their experience, then using that evidence in product and messaging decisions.
- [Discovery interview](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/discovery-interview.html): A discovery interview is a conversation meant to understand a problem, a workflow, or a job someone already has, before you shape a product.
- [Usability test vs customer interview](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/usability-test-vs-customer-interview.html): A usability test watches someone try a specific task in a product or design so you can see where they get stuck.
- [Saturation (qualitative research)](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/saturation.html): In qualitative research, saturation is the point at which new interviews repeat themes you already have, rather than adding new ones.
- [Leading question](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/leading-question.html): A leading question is a question that nudges the person toward a particular answer, often by smuggling in a preference, a cause, or a compliment.
- [Interview guide](https://nar-vardanyan.github.io/frank-mcp/glossary/interview-guide.html): An interview guide is a planned list of topics or questions for a research interview, usually in a consistent order, with room to follow up.
